::: course-content
[Workshop]{.course-badge}

## Follow-Up Workshop: ATAC-Seq Analysis

<p class="lead">

Join this in-person workshop hosted at the Hub for Applied Bioinformatics @KCL covering R-based ATAC-seq pipelines and multi-omic data integration. 

</p>

### About the Workshop

This three-hour in-person session serves as a practical follow-up to the [Innovation Scholars online workshop](https://learninghub.kingshealthpartners.org/course/ngs-atac-seq). 

Building directly on the data and R objects you generated during the online module, the critical decision-making steps along the ATAC-seq analysis pipeline will be examined. 

You will also learn how to integrate ATAC-seq results with other ‘omic’ datasets and leverage external genomic resources to uncover potential regulatory networks—using fast, accessible R-based tools alongside real-world case studies.

### What you will learn

By the end of this workshop, you will be able to independently conduct and critically analyse data from ATAC-seq experiments. 


### Audience

This workshop is designed for researchers, bioinformaticians, PhD students, and research staff who have completed the Innovation Scholars online ATAC-seq workshop and want to deepen their practical R skills for multi-omic integration and independent data analysis.

### Prerequisites

- Completion of the associated free online module, [**NGS: ATAC-seq**](https://learninghub.kingshealthpartners.org/course/ngs-atac-seq), is mandatory before attending the in-person workshop. It will take approximately 10 hours to complete the online materials. 
- Software Setup: RStudio installed on your laptop with all libraries from the online workshop pre-installed.
- Workshop Data: The .RDS data object generated during the online workshop.

For further information about the session, visit the [official workshop page](https://hab.sites.er.kcl.ac.uk/event/atac-seq-analysis/) or email hab@kcl.ac.uk

### Location 

The workshop will take place at the Hub for Applied Bioinformatics in the Hodgkins Building, Guy’s Campus.

The HAB space is located on the ground floor of the Hodgkin building at the Guy’s campus (room G60).

**Venue Details** Hodgkins Building, Guy’s Campus, Room G60, Newcomen St, London, SE1 1UL
